summary: Initial security posture and hosting intake. Bluecrest is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PHI-adjacent diagnostics inference. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + IdP mapping, KMS / HSM key control, audit log retention and tamper-resistance, and data residency for EU patients. AE/SE walked through Redwood hosting options and pointed to fallbacks and pilot plan. Action items agreed: share compliance artifacts, pilot config, and schedule RBAC/audit demo.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Elena Park, Marcus Yao (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Miguel Santos, Renee Park, Tommy Li (Bluecrest)

Summary: quick intake on security posture and hosting preferences for inference workloads at Bluecrest Diagnostics.

00:00 Elena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Elena from Redwood, and i think we have Marcus on the call as our solutions engineer. can you all introduce yourselves briefly?
00:12 Aisha Khan: hi i'm aisha, cto at bluecrest, we run a set of clinical inference pipelines, mostly deidentified but some workflows touch phi when we do retrospective chart pulls, so security is big for us.
00:26 Miguel Santos: miguel, head of security, i'll focus on compliance bits. we want to understand what evidence you can give and how keys/data are controlled.
00:34 Marcus Yao: great, quick note—Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. hosted is fastest, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, private is VPC or on‑prem. we can run through tradeoffs.
00:47 Renee Park: renee here, infra lead—my main questions are about networking, sso, and how audit logs look. we have strict retention policies for our EU clinics.
00:58 Elena Park: perfect, so top areas we'll cover: SOC two and ISO, sso/saml, rbac and granular access, audit logs and retention, and encryption / KMS, including BYOK/HSM. sound ok?
01:12 Tommy Li: yep, also curious about latencies and whether dedicated helps with tail latency.
01:19 Marcus Yao: good callout, latency vs cost is often a deciding factor. dedicated has predictable throughput and lower p99 in our benchmarks, but hosted can be cheaper at low volume. we'll share some perf tables.

03:05 Miguel Santos: regarding compliance, do you have a SOC2 type II report and ISO 27001? do you allow us to run audits or access audit artifacts?
03:16 Elena Park: yes we have SOC2 Type II and an ISO 27001 summary; i will send the redacted report and cert. for deeper audits we have an enterprise package - private deployments and additional audit support.
03:32 Miguel Santos: when you say private, do you mean a customer managed control plane with an on‑prem option? we need to ensure logs never leave our VPC.
03:41 Marcus Yao: with Redwood Private we can deploy the control plane in your VPC, logs and metrics can be stored in your side. the control plane still communicates with our ops plane for updates if you allow, but we also support air‑gapped installs for highly regulated customers. sometimes transcribed as "air gapped" which confuses people but yes we support on prem packages.

06:00 Aisha Khan: encryption—we need BYOK for encryption at rest and H S M backed keys. do you support K M S integrations like AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM?
06:12 Marcus Yao: yes, we support customer‑managed keys across major cloud KMS providers and can integrate with on‑prem H S M. we do key zeroization on deprovisioning. small note: sometimes the docs refer to it as "K M S swap" in older notes—ignore that.
06:30 Miguel Santos: what's the model for key access? do Redwood operators ever see plaintext?
06:35 Elena Park: no, we don't have access to plaintext tokens or model inputs in dedicated/private when BYOK is enabled. for hosted customers without BYOK we hold encrypted keys, but access is limited by RBAC and audit trails.

09:12 Renee Park: audit logs—we need immutable logs with tamper evidence and 7 year retention for certain data classes. can you push logs to our splunk or secure s3?
09:24 Marcus Yao: yes, audit logs can be exported via push to your logging infra, or kept in our service with configurable retention. for the private option you can keep everything inside your account. logs include request metadata, user id mapping, route, model/version, and redaction markers for PII. note: sometimes the transcript shows 'redaction maker'—that's a mis‑transcribe.
09:50 Miguel Santos: are the logs hashed or WORM? we need tamper resistance for regulatory audits.
09:56 Marcus Yao: we can sign logs and optionally put an append‑only chain in a customer bucket; for very strict scenarios we suggest putting logs into an H S M‑backed WORM store. we'll include the architecture notes in the followup.

12:20 Aisha Khan: SSO—our idp is Okta, and we require SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and role mapping. is that supported?
12:30 Elena Park: yes, SAML 2.0 + SCIM for user provisioning is supported. RBAC maps from IdP groups to Redwood roles. Marcus, can you run through typical role mapping?
12:42 Marcus Yao: sure—admin, engineer, viewer are typical roles; we support custom roles and least privilege rules. mapping from okta groups to custom roles is straightforward. small caveat: the metadata xml for SAML needs a certificate rotation step documented.
13:05 Renee Park: any gotchas around invalidation of sessions or token expiry for long running jobs?
13:12 Marcus Yao: we have session tokens and also token scopes for service accounts. for long‑running jobs you can use service tokens with restricted scopes that don't expire or rotate automatically through your KMS. there was a prior doc called "service principal flow" that some customers misread—we'll send the clearer guide.

16:40 Miguel Santos: data residency—some patient data must remain in EU. how do you handle regional routing or model variants?
16:51 Marcus Yao: Redwood's smart routing allows region pins; we also offer region‑specific model variants. for private deployments you can host inference entirely in your EU region or on‑prem. hosted api also supports region opts but you'll need data processing agreements.

19:10 Tommy Li: for the inference itself, is any cached prefix or KV cache stored with customer keys? we worry about leftover cached data in GPU memory or ephemeral stores.
19:25 Marcus Yao: KV cache is ephemeral in memory by default and not persisted to disk unless you enable cache warmup that writes to a customer bucket. when BYOK is on, persisted caches are encrypted under the customer's keys. there's a note in older transcriptions about "KV cash"—ignore that.

22:00 Aisha Khan: curious about compliance for the model artifacts themselves—do you vendor sign model binaries and provide provenance?
22:12 Elena Park: we provide model provenance and hashes for verified models in our catalog. for custom models loaded into Dedicated/Private we support signed images and an attestation process.

25:30 Miguel Santos: on the legal side, we need to see data processing agreements and how deletion requests are fulfilled. retention and deletion windows must be auditable.
25:42 Elena Park: absolutely—we have documented deletion workflows, and we log deletion events. for hosted customers we perform retention policies but for private/dedicated you can fully control those via config. we'll include our DPA and deletion playbook.

29:00 Renee Park: cost question—if we go dedicated what are minimum commitments and how fast can we scale for bursts?
29:12 Elena Park: dedicated is reserved with commits; burst capacity is configurable. typical pilots start with a 2‑week dedicated pool to validate throughput and cost, then move to monthly reserves. Marcus I'll follow up with example numbers.

32:45 Marcus Yao: (screen share ref) walk through of a sample pilot architecture: 2 nodes, model quantized to 8bit, KV cache enabled with encryption, network peering to your VPC, and a logging sink to your S3. this usually hits sub‑200ms median for shorter contexts in our tests but depends on model.
33:10 Tommy Li: sub‑200 median sounds good, but p99 matters to us. can you run a p99 benchmark under sustained load?
33:20 Marcus Yao: yes, pilot includes a benchmark plan—we'll run 95/99 latency under your workload shape. we'll need sample prompt sets and token distributions.

36:00 Miguel Santos: any third‑party attestations we should know about? pen tests, vuln scans, bug bounties?
36:10 Elena Park: we run regular internal vulnerability scans and periodic pentests with a third party; we can share a summary and remediation timelines. for enterprise there's an option for customer‑initiated pen tests under a scope.

39:30 Aisha Khan: last thing—who in your team will be our point of contact during pilot and for escalation?
39:40 Elena Park: i'll be the AE and program lead, Marcus will be the SE lead for technical work. for enterprise/private deployments we assign an implementation manager.

42:00 Miguel Santos: recap then: you will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, SAML/SCIM integration docs and metadata, pilot architecture + perf plan, and sample DPA + deletion playbook. also schedule a follow‑up RBAC+audit demo next week.
42:18 Elena Park: correct. i'll email the artifacts by tomorrow morning and propose times for the demo.
42:26 Renee Park: i'll assemble token volume estimates and our EU residency list and send by friday.

46:15 Elena Park: thanks everyone; we'll follow up in email w/ links to docs and the pilot doc.
46:22 Aisha Khan: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
